Hi Liam — thanks for the note and the docs. Quick responses below and next steps.

- Standard policy: our default hosted-plan payment term is Net30. For Enterprise/provisioned cases we evaluate Net45/Net60 on a case-by-case basis tied to credit reviews and a short ramp/advance requirement.
- VAT: we do pass-through VAT where applicable. For EU VAT-exempt routing (reverse charge) we need your VAT registration/EORI and a signed tax routing acknowledgement.
- Pilot asks: we can consider a provisional Net45 or Net60 on a staged basis — contingent on a short credit evaluation and a 2-invoice advance or payment guardrail while the pilot is active.

Next steps I propose:
1) Priyom / Marissa run a credit review on AcroMed and recommend a provisional credit ceiling.
2) We draft a 90-day amendment that documents: provisional term (Net45 or Net60), provisional credit limit, advance requirement (30% on first two invoices), VAT evidentiary items, and review cadence.
3) If agreed, we send via DocuSign for signatures.

I’m available for a 20m call Wednesday afternoon if that helps finalize. Attaching our credit request form so your finance team can fill in the missing pieces.

Best,

Quick credit results after running bank reference + AR aging + public filings: AcroMed presents as investment-grade for vendor credit in our risk model, but cash conversion timing is tight. My recommendation:

- Provisional credit limit: $1,200,000 for 90 days (pilot period).
- Payment terms: Net45 (compromise).
- Advance: 30% on Invoice #1 and Invoice #2 (applied as credit on following invoice).
- VAT/tax: require VAT registration copy and a signed tax routing acknowledgement. If they want Net60, propose a 60-day cooldown after the 90-day pilot with additional collateral (letter of credit or escrow).
- Monitoring: weekly invoice aging reports, 30/60/90-day reconciles; automatic downgrade to Net30 if >45 days past due on two consecutive invoices.

I’ve attached the scoring workbook and a redline summary of the proposed amendment. If everyone agrees, I can feed this into legal for a short, one-page amendment.
